tour.title: Core Types and Interfaces
tour.description: Start with the foundational type definitions that every other module depends on. This file defines the Plugin interface, EngineContext dependency injection container, ReconnectResult, and MediaAttachment types. With a fan-in of 17, it is the single most imported file in the codebase -- understanding these types is the prerequisite for reading everything else.

tour.title: AI Provider Abstraction
tour.description: Open Alice supports multiple AI backends behind a unified interface. The AIProvider type definitions establish the contract -- ask() for one-shot, generate() for streaming ProviderEvents -- while the Vercel AI SDK provider implements it with lazy model creation, hot-reload on config change, and streaming tool-call support. This adapter pattern lets you swap Claude, Vercel AI, or mock providers without touching domain code.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript discriminated unions (ProviderEvent is a union of {type: 'tool_use'}, {type: 'text'}, etc.) let the compiler narrow types in switch statements, eliminating runtime type checks.

tour.title: Session and Conversation Store
tour.description: Building on the core types from Step 1, this module manages conversation history as append-only JSONL files -- compatible with Claude Code's format. It provides both production (SessionStore) and in-memory (MemorySessionStore) backends, plus format converters that transform raw JSONL into Vercel AI SDK messages, text history, and chat history for the web UI. Eleven modules depend on it, making it the second-most-imported file.
tour.languageLesson: JSONL (JSON Lines) stores one JSON object per line, enabling append-only writes and streaming reads without loading the entire file. This is ideal for conversation logs where new messages are appended continuously.

tour.title: Unified Trading Account
tour.description: The UTA is the heart of the trading domain. Each account wraps a broker connection and layers on a git-like commit workflow: stage an order, commit with a message, push to execute. It also manages automatic health tracking with exponential-backoff recovery. The trading index barrel re-exports the full public API including account-manager, brokers, git, guards, and snapshot modules.
tour.languageLesson: The git-like trading metaphor (stage, commit, push) maps version control concepts to trade execution. This makes trade history auditable and reversible at the staging level, similar to how developers review code before merging.

tour.title: Broker Registry and Exchange Integration
tour.description: The broker registry enables dynamic self-registration: each broker implementation (CCXT for 100+ crypto exchanges, Alpaca for US equities, IBKR for institutional trading) registers its configSchema, configFields, and fromConfig factory. This allows the UI to render configuration forms automatically. The CCXT broker is the primary crypto adapter, implementing the full lifecycle from contract resolution to order placement, position tracking, and crypto-specific features like funding rates and liquidation summaries.

tour.title: Git Persistence and Trade History
tour.description: Trading-as-Git is a core design principle: all trade state is persisted as JSON files on disk with atomic write-then-rename for crash safety. The git sub-module exposes the TradingGit class that provides commit, log, and diff operations on the trading state. This makes the entire trade history auditable, diffable, and recoverable -- just like a git repository.

tour.title: Guard Pipeline and Risk Safety
tour.description: Before any trade executes, it must pass through the guard pipeline. Guards run in sequence: CooldownGuard enforces minimum intervals between trades on the same symbol, SymbolWhitelistGuard restricts trading to configured symbols. The pipeline wraps the dispatcher, so adding a new guard requires only registration -- no dispatcher changes. Complementing the guard pipeline, the kill switch provides emergency shutdown by reading a JSON flag file with fail-closed defaults.
tour.languageLesson: The guard pipeline follows the Chain of Responsibility pattern: each guard can approve or reject an operation, and the pipeline short-circuits on the first rejection. Fail-closed defaults (kill switch halts on malformed input) are a safety-first design principle in financial systems.

tour.title: Tool Bridge to AI
tour.description: The ToolCenter is the bridge between domain capabilities and the AI agent. All tool definitions are registered during bootstrap and exported in both Vercel AI SDK and MCP formats. This decoupling means domain code never imports AI provider modules -- the tool layer translates domain operations into the schema the AI understands.

tour.title: Strategy Factors and Regime Detection
tour.description: The strategy layer provides quantitative factor evaluation (momentum, volatility, volume profile, funding rate, liquidation pressure, liquidity imbalance) and ensemble combiners. The regime classifier evaluates threshold-based rules on volatility percentile, trend strength, and range compression to select between trend-follow, bear-trend, range-rotation, vol-stress, and spot-defensive regimes. Together they form the signal generation pipeline.

tour.title: Backtesting and Statistical Validation
tour.description: Before any strategy goes live, it must pass the backtest framework. Statistical significance testing includes PBO estimation, Deflated Sharpe Ratio, and SPA-like bootstrap p-values. Monte Carlo risk simulation uses IID and moving-block bootstrap methods to estimate profit probability, risk of ruin, and confidence intervals. The release gate blocks strategies that fail significance thresholds.
tour.languageLesson: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio adjusts for multiple testing bias -- when you test many strategies, some will appear profitable by chance. PBO (Probability of Backtest Overfitting) estimates how likely a strategy's performance is due to overfitting rather than genuine alpha.

tour.title: Web API and Real-Time Streaming
tour.description: The web connector exposes the entire system via Hono HTTP endpoints with Server-Sent Events for real-time streaming to UI clients. Sub-channel routing delivers events to the correct client session. The trading route alone handles account listing, position/order queries, market clock, quotes, and order placement -- all backed by the domain layer from Steps 4-6.
tour.languageLesson: Server-Sent Events (SSE) provide a one-way persistent connection from server to client over HTTP. Unlike WebSockets, SSE is unidirectional (server pushes to client), simpler to implement, and works through HTTP proxies. Each event is a text frame with an optional event type and data payload.

tour.title: React Dashboard
tour.description: The UI layer brings everything together in a React dashboard. App.tsx defines all page routes with React Router and manages sidebar navigation. ChatPage handles multi-channel conversations with streaming tool-call display via the useChat hook. TradingPage orchestrates account management, operator readiness monitoring, a multi-step create wizard, and edit dialogs for account settings -- the user-facing surface of the UTA from Step 4.
